x: SiteBoard Site reporting dashboard for the WP12 Pan Borneo Sabah Fasa 1B supervision team. It reads the daily Site Daily Photo Reports made in the SDR app and turns them into matrices, a structure board, a photo gallery and weekly / monthly reports.

How it works IOWs make the daily report in the SDR app and send the PDF. The report admin saves the PDFs in the shared Google Drive folder. Everyone opens SiteBoard in Chrome or Edge, connects the folder, and sees the same numbers. Report files never leave your computer. This website holds the program code only.

Team guide One page for everyone who uses the dashboard.

1. Who does what IOWs make the Site Daily Photo Report in the SDR app every working day and send the PDF to the report admin. REs and AREs report as required. Report admin (Resident Engineer) saves each PDF into the shared Google Drive folder. Nobody else changes files in that folder.

2. Filing rules Keep the file name exactly as the SDR app creates it, e.g. WP12-CST-MAT-20261016-1_SDR.pdf . Never rename or edit the PDF. Save into the current month folder, e.g. 2026-10 . If unsure, drop the file anywhere in the folder and press Tidy folder in Report files . A corrected report is generated again in the app, with the next number ( -2 ). The old file stays. Folders starting with _ or . are ignored by the dashboard.

3. Opening the dashboard (every team member) Use Chrome or Edge on a computer . Phones can view but cannot connect a folder. Install Google Drive for desktop , open its preferences and choose Mirror files so the folder is fully on your PC. Right-click the shared folder and make sure it is available offline. Open the SiteBoard link and press Connect reports folder . Choose the shared Drive folder (for example G:\My Drive\WP12\CST_Daily_Reports ). Press Allow . Keep the tab open: it checks the folder every 20 seconds. Next time, press Reconnect folder once.

t: 4. Daily routine for the report admin
x: 4. Daily routine for the report admin Check Overview and Submissions for missing reports. Use Missing-report message (Submissions) to remind IOWs on WhatsApp. Review Observations : set each to Open, Monitoring or Closed and add a note. At week end and month end use Generate report .

5. Sharing settings with the team Project details, who must report daily, non-working days and observation follow-up are stored in your browser. In Settings press Save settings to folder ; the file siteboard-settings.json then reaches every teammate through Google Drive and is read automatically.

6. If something looks wrong Open Report files : it lists files that could not be read, mismatches and duplicates. A report shows “not received” but was sent? Check it is in the folder and that Google Drive has finished syncing. Reports made by SDR v1.2.6 or later carry exact data inside the PDF; older ones are read from the page layout and may need a check.

7. Photos and structures Photos shows every photo. Filter by date, reporter, activity, structure, zone, chainage or text. Click a photo to enlarge it; use the arrow keys to move on. Prepare all thumbnails makes the gallery load instantly next time. Structures lists the bridges, culverts, junction culverts and RS walls with the last record, status and photos. See Structures and photos .
8. Today view Open Today first thing: who has reported, what was done, which structures were worked and the day's photos. It shows the latest report day if nothing has come in yet today.
Structures and photos

Structure board Lists the 4 bridges, 32 culverts, 13 junction culverts and 3 RS walls from the SDR setup.json , with state ( Active in the last 7 days, Recorded , No record ), last activity and status, number of records and photos. How a work item is matched to a structure Assigned by you (see below). Structure code written in the report (C12, JC3, B2, RSW1) – exact. Description and chainage when no code is written. SiteBoard reads the type (box or pipe), size, side and river name from the text, then picks the nearest structure of that type. The chainage limit is wide because drawing chainages are indicative and culverts are moved or offset on site: about 150 m for culverts, 100 m for juncti

Photo gallery Filter by date, reporter, activity category, structure, zone, chainage range and text, or show only items with remarks. The large view shows the details, a link to the report, a GPS link (reports from SDR v1.2.6+) and a download button.

Weekly and monthly reports Generate report builds an A4 report from the reports in the period: cover, summary, reporting matrix, works by category, progress by zone and chainage, structures referenced, weather, RFI references, site remarks, planned works and a photographic record with sign-off boxes. Choose Weekly or Monthly and the period. Fill in the report number, prepared / checked names and the planned works. Choose the photos (or let SiteBoard pick) and press Build . Press Print / Save as PDF and choose Save as PDF in the browser dialog. Keep Background graphics on. A logo can be added to the cover in Settings. The report is generated on your computer; nothing is uploaded. Export Excel
Administrator notes

Publishing the site (GitHub Pages) Create a public repository, for example siteboard . It holds code only – never reports, names or contractor details. Upload everything in this folder to the repository root (keep the .nojekyll file). Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → main / (root) . After a minute: the dashboard is at https://cstwp12-admin.github.io/siteboard/ and these notes at /docs/ . Open tools/build_docs.py , replace cstwp12-admin in the two addresses at the top, and rebuild the notes (below). Commit.

Editing these notes The pages are written in Markdown in docs-src/ . After editing, run python3 tools/build_docs.py (needs pip install markdown ) to rebuild docs/ , then commit both folders. The notes use the same design as the SDR app documentation.

Adding people Anyone with the link and the shared Drive folder can use it. Access to the reports is controlled by Google Drive sharing, not by SiteBoard. To give an assistant RE access, share the Drive folder with them.

Another work package Open the dashboard on that package's folder, set the project text in Settings, import that package's setup.json , and Save settings to folder . Nothing in the code needs to change.

Categories and wording The SDR setup (version 7: 52 structures, 193 activities) is built in, so the exact SDR activity names decide the category; anything not in the list falls back to the keyword rules in js/config.js . After the SDR setup changes, use Settings → Import SDR setup.json.

Ecosystem and wider use

The two apps The SDR app is the capture tool: one person, one day, one PDF with photos, chainage, activity, BQ, structure, RFI and GPS. SiteBoard is the monitoring tool: it reads every SDR PDF and shows the whole team and the whole project. Everything SiteBoard shows starts as an SDR report. Function Lives in Why Capture photos, GPS, activity, BQ, structure, chainage, RFI SDR it is the data-entry tool One-person daily PDF SDR Master lists (activities, structures, zones, centreline) SDR setup.json single source; SiteBoard imports it Team matrices, compliance, observation follow-up SiteBoard needs all reports together Weekly / monthly period reports SiteBoard combines many PDFs Structure board

Can the contractor use it? Yes, with the same code. It only needs a folder of SDR-format PDFs, so a contractor team that produces SDR reports can connect its own folder and get the same matrices, structure board, gallery and period reports. Points to settle first: - Keep the folders separate. The consultant's supervision records and the contractor's own records are different documents with different purposes. Each organisation connects its own folder and keeps its own settings file. - Team filter. x: Can it be the project reporting dashboard? For a project-level audience (client, SO, JKR) the current design has two limits: each person reads a local folder, and a phone cannot connect a folder. Two sensible routes, smallest first: 1. Snapshot page (recommended first step). SiteBoard exports one self-contained HTML page with the period's numbers and charts (reporting compliance, works by category, progress by zone, structure status, rain days, RFIs) and optionally selected photos. Share it by email, WhatsApp or Drive; it opens on any phone and needs no hosting, and nothing is published publicly. 2. Live shared dashboard.
